source.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States

accepted.question_text: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L × L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?

evidence.quote: Take a square region R of size n × n in the torus ... The Hamiltonian is then defined by translating hR, H = Στ τ(hR) ... The basic open question here is the following
Question 1 Which are the minimal requirements on A and the minimal size of R under which one can guarantee that the given PEPS is the unique ground state of H and in addition H is gapped?

accepted.question_text: Let T be a primitive quantum channel acting on D × D matrices, where the primitivity index p(T) is the smallest n such that T^n(ρ) has full rank for every positive semidefinite input ρ. What is the exact best possible upper bound on p(T) as a function of the dimension D?

evidence.quote: Definition 5 A quantum channel is called primitive if there exists an n ∈ N so that T^n(ρ) is full rank for all positive semi-definite input ρ. The minimum of such n is called the primitivity index p(T ).
Question 2 Which is the optimal upper bound for the primitivity index of a primitive quantum channel T acting on MD×D?

accepted.question_text: For a normal translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index, meaning the smallest scale at which the associated tensor becomes injective?

evidence.quote: Question 3 Which is the optimal upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal MPS in terms of its bond dimension?

accepted.question_text: For a normal projected entangled pair state (PEPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index?

evidence.quote: Question 4 Which is the optimal upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal PEPS in terms of its bond dimension?

accepted.question_text: Give an explicit and computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.

evidence.quote: As opposed to the 1D case, the only known result ... is the existence of a function of the bond dimension f(D) that bounds i(A) for every PEPS with bond dimension D. Unfortunately, in principle such function could be uncomputable.
Question 5 Give an explicit (computable and if possible polynomial) function f(D) which is an upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal PEPS.

accepted.question_text: Is the following bulk-boundary correspondence for PEPS exactly true: the parent Hamiltonian of a projected entangled pair state is gapped if and only if the corresponding boundary states can be written as Gibbs states of one-dimensional short-range Hamiltonians whose interaction terms decay exponentially with distance?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 The gap of the parent Hamiltonian of a PEPS corresponds exactly to the possibility of writing the boundary states as Gibbs states of 1D short range Hamiltonians
Question 6 Is Conjecture 1 true?

accepted.question_text: In two dimensions, does every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian admit a global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption alone, without any additional assumptions about the low-energy spectrum?

evidence.quote: Question 7 Does there exist a global approximation result in 2D only under the spectral gap assumption?

accepted.question_text: For the two-dimensional global PEPS approximation problem, can the bond-dimension bound f(L) required to approximate an L × L system be chosen to grow polynomially in the linear system size L?

evidence.quote: Question 8 Can the function f(L) be taken polynomial in L?

accepted.question_text: In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(ε) be chosen polynomial in 1/ε?

evidence.quote: Question 9 Does there exist a local approximation result in 2D? Is this possible assuming only the spectral gap assumption? Can g(ε) be taken polynomial in 1/ε?

accepted.question_text: Suppose two local tensors A and B define exactly the same projected entangled pair state on every L × L torus, meaning |Ψ_A⟩ = |Ψ_B⟩ for all system sizes. What local relation between A and B characterizes this equality of PEPS?

evidence.quote: Question 10 What is the relation between two tensors A and B that define the same PEPS, i.e. |ΨA⟩ = |ΨB⟩, on a torus L × L for all possible sizes L?

accepted.question_text: Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, interpolating between the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality is undecidable.

evidence.quote: Question 11 Give a Fundamental Theorem in 2D (and higher dimensions) for the largest possible family of PEPS.

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be PEPS tensors such that there exist ε > 0 and a size L0 with the property that for every L ≥ L0 the states they define on the L × L torus satisfy ‖|Ψ_A⟩ − |Ψ_B⟩‖² ≤ ε. Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between the tensors A and B?

evidence.quote: Question 12 Given A and B such that there exists an ε > 0 and a system size L0 such that for all L ≥ L0, ‖|ΨA⟩ − |ΨB⟩‖² ≤ ε, is there a local relation between both tensors?

accepted.question_text: For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?

evidence.quote: Question 13 Can one write the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC)-dimension for such ML algorithms as a function of the bond dimension?

accepted.question_text: What is the exact computational complexity class of the two-dimensional PEPS zero-testing problem?

evidence.quote: Question 14 Which is the exact complexity class for 2D PEPS zero-testing?

accepted.question_text: Given a finite group G and a normal subgroup H, does there exist a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H?

evidence.quote: Question 15 Is there a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to a finite group G to the one associated to a normal subgroup H?

accepted.question_text: What is the exact relationship between projected entangled pair states and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions?

evidence.quote: Question 16 Which is the exact relation between PEPS and QCA in 2D and higher dimensions?
